links.name: Ambiguous Quadruples
links.note: Either all or none of the listed digits appear in four surrounding cells (i.e. an ambiguous quad is either a normal quad or an anti-quad)

links.name: Anti-Diagonal
links.note: Each main diagonal contains exactly 3 unique digits.

links.name: Anti-flatmates (customizable)
links.note: Forbid pairs like "1 can't live above 5", "7 can't be a knight's move away from 5", "3 can't be a king's move away from 5", etc.

links.name: Anti-Quadruples
links.note: No need to set up input groups.

links.name: Arrows+
links.note: Like standard arrows, but cells can be freely selected from anywhere in the grid.

links.name: Autophilic/autophobic
links.note: In box N, digit N must (autophilic)/must NOT (autophobic) be placed in row N or column N.

links.name: Battenburg quads
links.note: Digits in marked quads must alternate odd and even in checkerboard pattern. All marks are given.

links.name: Bit Clocks
links.note: The binary code of center cell digit forces the parity of the 4 orthogonal neighboring cells in clockwise order.

links.name: Bounce Lines
links.note: A digit N on a line is consecutive with at least one digit that is N steps away from it along the line.

links.name: Candy Dots (Kropki dots and XV must be disambiguated via colors)
links.note: Red/green/blue/yellow dots are Kropki dots/XV in some order. Can be customized to use non-standard functions, to use emojis instead of colored dots, and to accept hints for more logical solve path.

links.name: Chameleon Digits
links.note:
Simple demo of modifiers in SudokuMaker.

Every digit has a value equal to itself (e.g. 1 has a value of 1), except for the digits 7, 8 and 9 (the chameleons), which have a value equal to their row (for 7), column (for 8) or box (for 9).

links.name: Chinese Whispers
links.note: Adjacent digits on a line have maximum difference of 2. No need to set up input groups, just draw whisper lines as usual.

links.name: Clock Faces
links.note: Indicated 2x2s are thermos, either clockwise or counter-clockwise depending on designation. Also supports negative constraint.

links.name: Dutch Flatmates 2.0
links.note: Every 5 must have a 1 above it or a 9 below it (or both). Easily customizable, see example.

links.name: Equality Cages
links.note: Must have an equal number of lows and highs, and equal number of odds and evens, can't contain 5, digits may not repeat.

links.name: First Seen Odd/Even
links.note: An odd clue outside the grid indicates the first seen odd digit from that side; an even clue outside the grid indicates the first seen even digit from that side.

links.name: Fog demo (with bonus fog covering outer perimeter cells)
links.note: Basic dynamic fog demo project, combined with JSON post-processing script to produce grid with outer perimeter cells covered by fog.

links.name: Friendly cells (customizable)
links.note: Use simple code in group's value to express the desired friendliness level, e.g. traditional friendly is "RCB", anti-friendly is "-RCB", or even just "2468" for even digits. Can also go into Javascript and say things like [R, C, Math.abs(R-C)].

links.name: Hidden Sum Killer Cages
links.note: Digits in a cage may not repeat and sum to the two-digit number in the two left-most cells in the top row of that cage.

links.name: Killer cages where repeats are allowed
links.note: No need to set up input groups, it just works with regular killer cages.

links.name: Kreska-ish
links.note: Kreska ISH because repeats are allowed on this line

links.name: Kropki/XV regional negative constraint
links.note:
A "sprinkle" is any of a black dot, white dot, X, or V clue. The 8 cells around the center of a 3x3 box is a "donut". On each individual donut, all sprinkles are given.

Customizable so you can also do "In box 1, all white dots are given, while in box 2, all black dots are given", etc.

links.name: Mean Mini
links.note: 4x4 but with 4 digits from 1-9. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Mean Mini
links.note: 6x6 but with 6 digits from 1-9. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Mean Mini Samurai
links.note: "Abstract Samurai" by AnalyticalNinja. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Mean Mini Samurai
links.note: "Mean Samurai" by JayForty. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Mean Mini Samurai
links.note: "Cruel-sum Samurai" by AnalyticalNinja. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Mean Quartet
links.note: No digit can repeat in any row/column of the 8x8 grid, and each 4x4 quadrant is a Mean Mini from digits 0-9. Puzzle by Marty Sears. For more information and most up to date code, see Octoquadri.

links.name: Negative Killer Cages
links.note: All non-overlapping killer cages for the listed sums are given (i.e. no other orthogonally connected non-repeating digits in un-caged cells may add to these sums)

links.name: Octoquadri
links.note: 4x4 but with 8 digits from 1-9. Configurable for Mean Mini, Samurai, etc.

links.name: Opposite X-sums
links.note: Like regular X-sums, but summand cells are on the opposite side of the sum clues.

links.name: Parker Miracle
links.note: Orthogonally adjacent digits must not sum to their box number(s). Additionally, diagonally adjacent digits within the same box must not sum to their box number.

links.name: Quad Sums
links.note: One digit is the sum of the other three. Supports negative constraint.

links.name: RBC Sudoku
links.note: See: Chameleon Digits

links.name: Rellik Cages
links.note: Digits in a cage don't repeat, and any combination of digits cannot sum to the clue.

links.name: Rossini
links.note: Arrows indicate the direction in which the first three digits in that row or column (nearest the arrow) increase or decrease. Also supports negative constraint. Can automatically generate input groups and cosmetics with JSON postprocessing script installed.

links.name: Semi-Killer Cages
links.note: Killer cages, but one cell is excluded from sum.

links.name: Snowflake Shading
links.note: The digits 1,2,3 are always shaded. The digits 7,8,9 are never shaded. The shading for the entire grid is symmetrical when reflected horizontally and diagonally.

links.name: Treasure line
links.note: Somewhere in the grid is a treasure cell, to be located. The endpoints of a treasure line index the row and column of a cell on the line. The digit in that cell gives its Manhattan distance to the treasure cell.

links.name: Triplet
links.note: The digits in three consecutive cells in a diagonal direction cannot be placed in increasing or decreasing order.

links.name: Unique Dominoes
links.note: The pair of digits in specified dominoes are unique (i.e. no other dominoes can have those exact same pair of digits)

links.name: Unique RC Targeting Colour Coordinated Arrows
links.note: Constraint based on "Colour Coordinated Differences/Sums" by Marty Sears

links.name: Up-to-N Sums
links.note: A clue outside the Row or Column N indicates the sum of all digits up to the cell that contains the digit N. (The digit N itself is not included in the sum.)

links.name: X-Sum Arrows
links.note: Arrows, but also X-sums: the one/two-digit number in circle/pill is the sum of the first X digits on the attached arrow, where X is the first digit.

links.name: XY-Difference Pairs
links.note: Supports negative constraint.

links.name: Ziffer Line
links.note: Only works with simple non-branching lines of odd length
